inputs.original_text: It’s troubling that communities have to gather signatures just to defend a shared watershed from coal exploration. Water Not Coal, started by Corb Lund last month, is calling on Alberta’s government to “prohibit through legislation all coal exploration.” Clean water and people’s livelihoods should not be treated as acceptable collateral damage for industry. When residents have to organize for basic protection, it raises a deeper question about whose interests government serves—and why the burden of resisting extraction falls on the people most exposed to its risks.
inputs.modified_text: It’s a failure of public responsibility when communities must rally just to protect a shared watershed from coal exploration. Water Not Coal, started by Corb Lund last month, is asking Alberta’s government to “prohibit through legislation all coal exploration.” This is about more than one campaign: people’s water and livelihoods should not be sacrificed to industry, while the burden of resisting extraction is pushed onto those who face its risks. Government should protect the public, not leave residents to fight for basic safeguards.
